scenes.label: 01 / ORIENTATION
scenes.title: Social Watch Space API
scenes.dek: A Java 17 / Spring Boot 3.3 backend for authenticated rooms, live room events, and timeline questions with citations.
scenes.note: This is a presentation layer for the backend project. The repository intentionally has no production frontend.

scenes.label: 02 / THE PROBLEM
scenes.title: Shared viewing needs a source of truth.
scenes.dek: A watch room needs more than a player: it needs identity, membership, host decisions, room events, and enough timeline context to answer questions responsibly.

cards.title: IDENTITY
cards.text: Know who is allowed to create, join, and act inside a room.

cards.title: ROOM BOUNDARY
cards.text: Keep membership and host ownership on the server, across REST and WebSocket paths.

cards.title: CONTEXT
cards.text: Retrieve the nearby timeline and show which source events support an answer.

scenes.callout: The implemented slice establishes these contracts. It does not claim synchronized playback is finished.

scenes.label: 03 / ARCHITECTURE
scenes.tag: A SMALL SERVICE WITH CLEAR EDGES
scenes.title: One backend. Five responsibilities.
scenes.dek: The service is organized into API contracts, domain state, application services, security, and transport adapters.

layers.name: SECURITY
layers.detail: Spring Security · JWT filters · ownership checks

layers.name: TRANSPORT ADAPTERS
layers.detail: WebFlux HTTP · typed WebSocket protocol · JDBC

scenes.footer: Blocking JDBC work is kept off reactive event-loop threads; reads return detached snapshots rather than mutable cached rooms.

scenes.label: 04 / IDENTITY
scenes.title: Identity is a token. Ownership is a room fact.
scenes.dek: Register, log in, and refresh JWT access tokens. Then let the room's server-side hostUserId authorize host operations.

steps.title: REGISTER / LOGIN
steps.detail: Creates a VIEWER account and issues access + refresh tokens.

steps.title: BEARER TOKEN
steps.detail: Authenticated API calls carry Authorization: Bearer <token>.

steps.title: ROOM CHECK
steps.detail: Membership and hostUserId are checked for the specific room.

guards: A global VIEWER role is not trusted as room ownership.
A client cannot promote itself by changing a JWT claim or request body.
WebSocket query-string tokens are rejected; the upgrade uses an Authorization header.

scenes.label: 05 / ROOM LIFECYCLE
scenes.title: Create. Join. Start. Lock. End.
scenes.dek: The host can move a room through its lifecycle, while membership operations remain explicit and server-authorized.

phases.name: CREATE
phases.detail: Authenticated creator becomes the room host.

phases.name: JOIN
phases.detail: Join by room id or secure invite code.

phases.name: START
phases.detail: Host starts a room after membership checks.

phases.name: LOCK
phases.detail: Host controls whether new joins are accepted.

phases.name: END
phases.detail: Host ends the room; later access is rejected.

scenes.callout: Invalid transitions return a conflict. Non-members receive forbidden. Host operations use the room's hostUserId.

scenes.label: 06 / ROOM EVENTS
scenes.title: Room events move through a typed gate.
scenes.dek: Authenticated clients connect to /api/v1/ws/watch-spaces/{id}, join first, then exchange validated JSON events.
checks: Bounded payloads, request ids, chat, and seek values
Stable error events for malformed messages
64-message queue per connection; slow overflow closes with 1013
scenes.truth: The registry is process-local. WebSockets forward commands, but do not maintain synchronized playback state, an authoritative clock, replay, or reconnect resynchronization.

scenes.label: 07 / PERSISTENCE
scenes.title: PostgreSQL is the default profile's durable edge.
scenes.dek: Accounts, rooms, participants, titles, and timeline events are stored through JDBC. Flyway owns the schema history.
properties: Room mutations use database row locks and transactions.
Reads return detached snapshots, not mutable cached rooms.
Tests use isolated H2 databases in PostgreSQL mode; a native PostgreSQL server check is still open.

scenes.label: 08 / TIMELINE AI
scenes.title: Ask the timeline. Show the evidence.
scenes.dek: The seeded demo-title timeline can answer membership-protected questions with excerpts and source-event citations.
scenes.question: Who is Detective Rios?
scenes.answer: Returns answer text, confidence, generatedAt, and source-event citations.
retrieval: Deterministic keyword retrieval, not a live Gemini model
With a position, search the preceding 120 seconds — never future events
Up to three citations, confidence, and generatedAt are returned
No matching event returns an insufficient-context response
scenes.disclosure: Confidence is an uncalibrated heuristic, not a probability. Gemini environment settings are reserved and currently unused.

scenes.label: 09 / PROOF + GAPS
scenes.title: A tested slice, honestly framed.
scenes.dek: The latest combined Maven check records the implemented behavior. The remaining gaps are part of the project story, not hidden behind the demo.
coverage: HTTP registration, create / join, and host authorization
JDBC rollback / read-back, migration, and timeline filtering
Citation retrieval and real multi-client WebSocket tests
Blocking work stays off reactive event-loop threads
gaps: Native PostgreSQL verification, Docker exercise, load / latency benchmark
Authoritative playback, drift correction, reconnect snapshots, cross-instance fan-out
Refresh rotation / revocation, rate limiting, admin enforcement, and observability
Validated admin timeline ingestion and a real grounded model integration

scenes.label: 10 / CLOSE
scenes.title: A clean boundary between what works and what comes next.
scenes.dek: The project has a concrete room protocol, durable persistence path, and cited timeline retrieval — with production hardening still named plainly.
